_comment: Calibration code -> bike. `code` is a prefix (the family); whatever follows it in a full code is the revision, so one entry covers 23ECCLGPSMB/MC/MD and `revisions` names the ones we know. Longest matching prefix wins; "match":"exact" beats any prefix. `space` says which identity the code belongs to: "image" = the calibration code inside a firmware file, "live" = the Drawing field of the 0x1A 0x80 response, "both" = we do not know which. They are NOT interchangeable — a Ducati answers 96520610B live while its image holds a calibration mnemonic. Keep `model` identical for entries describing the same bike: the write guard compares brand+model, so splitting one bike across two model strings would hard-block a legitimate flash. Anything not read off a real ECU or image here carries "verified": false. Entries added from the UI land in /etc/onboard-logger/fw_catalog.json as an overlay and carry "user": true; this file stays the seed and keeps growing with updates. Entries with "guard": false are reference only: they name a bike in the UI but never resolve a side for the write guard, because their model text comes from a free-form tune list where one motorcycle appears under several names.
